items.statement: Published evidence shows extended pharmacy hours are close to cost-neutral for the payer only when at least a fifth of late users would otherwise have attended an emergency department.
items.rationale: The decision turns on the counterfactual; the review can show where the break-even lies across the retrieved and further studies.
items.risks: Too few studies report the counterfactual.

items.statement: Extended hours mainly benefit shift workers and people without a registered GP, and their value depends on location near late public transport.
items.rationale: Supported by user logs and public views; decides where the 40 pharmacies should be.
items.risks: User data come from pharmacist logs rather than users.

items.statement: Schemes without shared rotas or security measures lose pharmacies within a year.
items.rationale: Owners reduced hours in one study.

summary: Three working propositions for the review; h1 selected for the budget strand, h2 and h3 carried into the practice strand.
